source.version_note: Published article, Group Decision and Negotiation 35:71, 2026; accepted 21 September. Supplied main article contains no online appendices.

citation.title: Is There a Human Premium in Negotiations? A Relational-Economic Tradeoff in Human vs. AI Bargaining

reading.source_scope_note: Randomized identity-description experiment with human students negotiating against GPT-4. Estimates concern assignment to human versus AI descriptions, not a verified contrast in every participant's beliefs, actual human-versus-model behaviour or an identified psychological mediator.
access_limits: All 16 main-article pages read, including assignment check, corrected hypothesis tests, exploratory analyses, limitations and references.

Online appendices A–D, full instructions/prompts, transcripts, coding details and promised repository data were not independently obtained or analyzed. Cited primary studies were not read as part of this file review.

study.sample: Undergraduates, mean age 19.88, SD 1.61, 63% female, class-credit laboratory participation
study.actual_counterpart: GPT-4 broker in both conditions, instructed to maximize rent
study.task: Simulated apartment rent negotiation; listing $2350, area comparison $1800–2400; optional extras mentioned
study.H1_correction: Benjamini–Hochberg across five counterpart evaluations: warmth and integrity retained; competence, ability and benevolence not significant after correction

summary: Add a context-specific human premium in negotiation: a human description increased relational evaluations and agreed simulated rent relative to an AI description. Keep it distinct from choosing to use algorithmic advice and from a verified mediation or general rule that humans obtain better overall outcomes. Preserve the substantial assignment-check ambiguity.

findings.definition: Giving a negotiation counterpart more favorable relational evaluations or economic concessions when it is described as human rather than AI.
findings.novelty_rationale: An explicitly named, context-specific outcome pattern, rather than a newly identified independent mechanism. Distinct from algorithm aversion's reluctance to choose or accept algorithmic judgment: participants here all bargain with a counterpart and differ in evaluation and negotiated terms. Related framing and mind-attribution accounts are possible explanations, not exact synonyms.

findings.evidence_scope: 205 students randomized to a purported human broker or AI broker, with GPT-4 actually used in both groups. Human-described mean rent $2129.58 versus AI-described $2054.20, d=.55; relational satisfaction d=.52. Warmth and integrity survived correction, while competence did not. The post-task item measured reported assignment, not in-task beliefs, and 42/96 in the person condition selected bot.
findings.boundary: This is an assignment-based, single simulated negotiation result, not proof every participant believed the description, a universal human advantage or irrational favoritism. The broker gains from higher rent while the participant pays more, but relational satisfaction can be a legitimate goal. Same underlying system does not mean identical interactive dialogue. Relational framing, mind perception, concessions and warmth-mediated effects were not causally isolated. Do not infer actual rent payments, long-term cooperation or a model's feelings.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Direct human identity-description experiment with an AI counterpart; context-specific outcome pattern, mediator and generality unestablished
findings.ai_proposal: Test effects of accurate counterpart disclosures on negotiated terms, subjective value and subsequent real cooperation. Log the actual dialogue and negotiated extras, distinguish assignment from measured beliefs, and use matched system behavior and appropriately consequential outcomes. Preserve truthful identity disclosure; do not deploy deceptive human labels to obtain concessions.

findings.term: Identity description is not an isolated anthropomorphic-cue intervention
findings.definition: Describing an actual AI counterpart as a person can alter evaluations without isolating the psychological process of attributing human traits to an entity known to be nonhuman.
findings.novelty_rationale: Separates explicit source description, attributed capacities and anthropomorphic design, which the article itself distinguishes in its limitations.

findings.evidence_scope: The same underlying text broker was presented under two descriptions. Perceived warmth, competence and trustworthiness were measured afterward; no randomized mind-perception mediator or embodied-cue factorial test was conducted.
findings.boundary: Believing the counterpart actually is human is not identical to projecting human traits onto a known machine. Evaluation differences do not prove machine experience, a causal warmth pathway or that all warmth cues induce undue trust.

methodological_limits: Randomization identifies effects of the assigned description under this protocol. The post-outcome item asked reported assignment, not contemporaneous belief: 95/109 AI-assigned and only 54/96 person-assigned selected the assigned identity. Do not reclassify or exclude participants post hoc without a justified analysis.

Both groups used the same GPT-4 negotiation system, but participants' messages and resulting responses can differ. This is not identical content with only a post-hoc source label, nor a comparison with actual human brokers.

The precise GPT-4 snapshot, generation settings and all constraints are not in the supplied main article. Prompts/transcripts are external. Their equivalence and the system's constraint compliance were not independently checked.

Students receiving class credit in one-shot simulated rent bargaining are not representative of professional negotiators. No actual rental payment, repeat negotiation, realized cooperation or financial incentive tied to rent is reported in the supplied text.

All 205 are said to complete the negotiation and survey, but relational satisfaction uses t(189), implying fewer usable observations for that test under the apparent independent-sample analysis. The main article does not explain that denominator; appendices are needed.

The paper says measures were specified a priori but does not present a preregistration in the supplied text. Five H1 outcomes are corrected together; exploratory framing, factor, sentiment and recommendation analyses should remain labeled exploratory.

After H1 correction, warmth adjusted p=.017 and integrity p=.004 remain; competence p=.065, ability p=.104 and benevolence p=.129 do not. Do not summarize all counterpart qualities as reliably higher.

Relational satisfaction and final rent are measured after one interaction. Their association cannot establish that warmth, relational concern or perceived mind caused concessions. The limitations explicitly note economic outcomes were not associated with warmth/benevolence/openness in the reported correlations.

Separate exploratory factor solutions for groups of 96 and 109 are descriptive and do not constitute a measurement-invariance test, a formal comparison of latent complexity or causal evidence of richer human representations.

Open-ended partnership/transactional coding, independent AI-coder checks and exact reliability are in an unread appendix. The two reported frame percentages do not sum to 100% within groups, so do not assume an exhaustive mutually exclusive binary without the codebook.
The single forward-looking item asks recommendation to a friend. Describing it as willingness to work with the broker again broadens the measure; neither wording establishes actual future engagement.

Final rent omits a complete valuation of optional gym or other extras and relational utility. Lower rent is a narrower economic outcome, not necessarily higher joint surplus, fairness, decision quality or long-term welfare.
The promised public repository is not linked in the supplied data statement, and raw data were not reanalyzed. No result beyond the supplied article's reported statistics is claimed.

cross_paper_learning.finding: The MCQ study confounded label with block order; this negotiation experiment randomizes the identity description, strengthening assignment-based inference. However, interactive content is not fixed and the identity check remains ambiguous.

Preference for a human decision-support tool differs from concessions to a purported human bargaining counterpart. Keep their related social explanations connected without counting the outcomes as synonyms or declaring all economic sacrifice irrational.

deferred.reason: A broad secondary framework of perceived agency and experience, already connected to existing mentalizing, anthropomorphism and sociomorphism coverage. This study does not isolate it as the mediator; no extra independent mechanism ID added here.
Exploratory factor label for warmth, benevolence, integrity and openness, not a newly validated standalone behaviour.
Description of separate exploratory factor solutions; no formal latent-structure comparison establishes a distinct cognitive mechanism.

limitations: One named, context-bound outcome pattern added, with no claim it is an independent causal mechanism or universal human bias.
No model moral psychology, verified in-task belief effect, actual economic payment or longitudinal relationship outcome inferred.
